# 5 Useful Sleeping Tips

## 1. Maintain a Consistent Sleep Schedule
- Regulates your body's internal clock (circadian rhythm)
- Makes falling asleep and waking up easier over time
- Improves overall sleep quality by training your brain to expect rest at specific times
- Reduces the grogginess associated with irregular sleep patterns

## 2. Limit Screen Time Before Bed
- Blue light from devices suppresses melatonin production
- Stimulating content keeps your brain alert and engaged
- Scrolling habits can lead to unintentional late nights
- Reduces mental stimulation, allowing your mind to wind down naturally

## 3. Keep Your Bedroom Cool (65-68°F / 18-20°C)
- Your body temperature naturally drops when falling asleep
- A cooler environment supports this biological process
- Prevents overheating and night sweats that disrupt sleep
- Promotes deeper, more restorative sleep stages

## 4. Avoid Caffeine After Early Afternoon
- Caffeine has a half-life of 5-6 hours, meaning it stays in your system long after consumption
- Blocks adenosine, the chemical that makes you feel sleepy
- Can reduce total sleep time even if you fall asleep successfully
- May decrease the amount of deep sleep you experience

## 5. Create a Relaxing Pre-Sleep Routine
- Signals to your brain that it's time to transition to sleep mode
- Reduces stress and anxiety that can cause insomnia
- Activities like reading or stretching lower heart rate and blood pressure
- Builds a positive psychological association between the routine and restful sleep
